summary.headline: Heritage Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% to INR13,381 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% on raw milk costs and a VAP mix shift.
summary.overview: Heritage reported record quarterly revenue of INR13,381 million (up 18% YoY), with EBITDA of INR619 million (4.6% margin) and PAT of INR150 million (1.9% margin). Value-added products (VAP) grew 40% YoY to INR5,636 million and reached a record 44% of revenue, while milk procurement cost rose 7% YoY to INR46.61 per litre. Management said the margin squeeze came from buffalo milk shortages, cow milk inflation, SMP usage and packaging costs, and that price hikes were continuing into July. Milk procurement volume grew only 2% and liquid milk volume growth remains the stated top priority.

financial_highlights.metric: Broader VAP incl. consumer ghee and butter

financial_highlights.change: +7% YoY; vs INR46.67 in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Milk
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 3.03% vs 5.8% a year ago; procurement volume up 2% YoY to 18.10 lakh litres per day, while milk sales volume was broadly stable. Cow milk procurement rose to about INR43.2 per litre from INR42.10 in Q4 FY26, and buffalo milk to INR65.99 from INR61.38, with buffalo volumes down over 20%.

segments.name: Value-added products (VAP)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR5,636 million, up 40% YoY, with about 5.12% weighted average price increase and the balance volume-driven. Paneer grew 33%, curd 26%, ice cream 25%, buttermilk 60%, lassi 98%. VAP EBITDA margin 8.06%. Curd is about 68.9% of VAP, down from about 75% previously.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Revenue above INR550 million, up 65% YoY; Alpenvie grew 44%. Newly commissioned facility ran at about 40% utilisation and now makes both Alpenvie and Get-A-Way from a common platform. Management said ice cream is the most profitable VAP.

segments.name: Ghee (consumer pack)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin about minus 8.5%, improved from about minus 12% a year earlier, but still loss-making.

segments.name: Heritage Nutrivet (animal nutrition)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR728 million, up 37% YoY, with PBT of INR20 million despite higher input costs; cattle feed raw material inflation is continuing.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of 16-17% growth, requiring milk volume growth of about 7-8% and VAP growth of about 25%.
Target to raise VAP share of revenue by 2-2.5 percentage points a year, reaching around 50% by FY30 from about 39% in FY26.
Long-term aim is high single-digit EBITDA margin rather than 6%; management cited a historical median of 7-7.5%.
FY27 capex of about INR250 crore covering paneer and ghee projects plus minor raw milk procurement capex.
Management declined to guide Q2 margins; said Q2 cattle feed (Nutrivet) margin pressure looks heavier, but Nutrivet's Q2 is expected to be slightly stronger than Q1.
Management expects buffalo flush around October-November; procurement prices seen stable to firm into Q2, with no easing as of July.
capex_capacity: Ice cream facility commissioned and ramped to about 40% utilisation in Q1 FY27; serves Alpenvie and Get-A-Way from a common platform.
Paneer and ghee projects under construction; FY27 capex about INR250 crore including minor raw milk procurement investment.
Heritage Novandie Foods became a wholly owned subsidiary (Livo high-protein yogurt brand); stake in Peanut Butter and Jelly Limited raised to 71%.
Farmer base grew by about 5,000 in Q1 and a further 5,000 is targeted in Q2 via village-level procurement centres.
Distribution network expanded through new distributors and Heritage happiness points; liquid milk added about 1 lakh litres per day in the quarter.
demand_pricing: VAP volume growth: about 80% of growth from distribution expansion in existing geographies, about 20% from consumer traction and market share gains in organised channels; no new geography opened.

Price hikes: about 4% on milk and 5.12% weighted average on VAP in Q1; hikes were staggered by market, with some in mid-May and others in early June, and further increases were taken in the week of the call.

Gross margin fell about 2.5 percentage points YoY, attributed to mix shift to cow milk, about 0.5% impact from higher-priced SMP consumed in larger quantities, and about 30 basis points from packaging material costs linked to the war.
Liquid milk volume growth remains weak; management says it is the highest-priority problem and that March-July shows month-on-month recovery.
Paneer contributed about INR52 crore of Q1 revenue and is non-seasonal; yogurt about 150 tonnes in the quarter.
Management said operating costs fell to 9.01% of revenue from 9.64% and employee costs to 6.74% from 7.21%, a combined operating leverage gain of about 1.1 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Is the flush season delayed and are milk prices easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the expected April-May mini flush did not materialise; prices rose from March to June and are now stable, with the October flush the next key point. Heritage added farmers at village level and is seeking higher throughput per farmer.

qa_highlights.question: Why has milk procurement been flat to negative for four quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement is planned on material balance and grew in line with demand; the industry is short of milk, and the company is investing in village collection centres and farmer productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Will VAP growth of 20-25% guidance change after the 40% quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 benefited from a low base after rain-hit Q1 FY26; the sustained long-term aim is 25% VAP growth and 16-17% total growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin decline despite a higher VAP mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Buffalo milk volumes fell over 20%, cow milk costs rose about INR1 per litre, SMP costs added about 0.5%, and packaging added about 30 basis points to the margin hit.

qa_highlights.question: Where are consumer packs and new geographies on breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghee EBITDA improved to minus 8.5% from minus 12% a year ago. Management said loss-making regions narrowed their losses, which avoided about INR1 crore of additional hit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY30 VAP and margin outlook, and how far can margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 50% VAP share by FY30 and high single-digit EBITDA. Raw milk prices are a major driver, with about three-quarters of revenue tied to raw material costs.

risks_watch: Milk price inflation: cow milk up about INR1 per litre QoQ and buffalo up about INR4.6; the El Nino year and weak October flush risk further pressure.
Margin compression: Milk EBITDA 3.03%, consolidated EBITDA 4.6%; Q2 margin not guided.
Liquid milk volume growth remains weak, which limits overhead absorption.
Cattle feed input inflation (Nutrivet) and packaging cost increases linked to the war.
Consumer price elasticity and competitive response to repeated price hikes; ghee remains loss-making at minus 8.5% EBITDA.
Watch for procurement volume growth matching VAP growth (procurement grew only 2%) and whether ice cream utilisation rises above 40%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on VAP growth, brand momentum and long-term strategy, but cautious and at times evasive on near-term margins and procurement prices, declining to guide Q2 or to give best and worst case price scenarios. Management repeatedly called the milk price environment unpredictable and said the company is in the "trough" of the cycle.
key_quotes: Consolidated revenue increased 18% year-on-year to INR13,381 million, marking another important milestone for Heritage.
So it's largely volume-driven growth and prices contributed about 5%.
So I should admit that this is the main problem that we need to solve.
So at this point in time, I should say that we are in the trough of it.

growth.why: Long-term 16-17% growth target held, requiring ~7-8% milk volume and ~25% VAP growth; Q1 revenue rose 18%, with VAP up 40% driven mostly by distribution expansion, but the plan rests on partly specified capacity (ice cream ramp at ~40%, paneer/ghee projects in FY27 capex of ~INR250 crore) and buffalo milk supply is down over 20%.
